meta.purpose: convergence evidence for BMC Medical Research Methodology's 'well tested' requirement: replicate doubling, grid refinement, and delta_sig resolution
meta.seed_derivation: sha256 over a namespaced cell key; the built-in hash() is avoided because PYTHONHASHSEED randomises it per process
meta.why_step4_and_step5_numbers_are_not_reus: those steps consume one stream across the grid in traversal order, so an inserted cell shifts every later cell; measured on the type I rows, one inserted cell moved 33 of 40 shared cells
meta.paired_se_derivation: nested streams make the difference depend on the last R draws only, so se = sqrt(rate_R (1 - rate_R) / R), not the sqrt(2)-larger unpaired value
meta.bounds: convergence of a Monte Carlo estimate is not validity of the estimand

block_R_replicate_doubling.design: type I cells, R = 2000 against 2R = 4000, nested streams, one stream per cell derived from its key

block_G_grid_refinement.design: midpoint insertion on p0 and on se, giving a strict superset; analytic quantities compared exactly, the type I error resampled on both grids

monotonicity.consequence: delta_tip is monotone in each axis, so its extremes over a box are attained at the vertices; inserting midpoints of p0 and se adds no vertex, so the extremes cannot move. Verified numerically below rather than only argued.

block_D_delta_sig_resolution.design: located crossing recomputed with 34 bisection iterations and 16000 replicates against 26 and 8000; n in {1000, 2000}
block_D_delta_sig_resolution.selection_note: every 20th eligible cell in file order, so the spread covers the grid rather than its first rows

checks.question: does the 2R stream literally extend the R stream?
checks.why_it_matters: the paired standard error sqrt(p(1-p)/R) is only correct under nesting. Under independent streams the error is sqrt(2) larger and every z below is understated by about 41 per cent

checks.question: does consuming a decoy draw first change the cell result?
checks.why_it_matters: this is the property steps 4 and 5 lack. Without it a grid-refinement comparison cannot separate a change in the estimate from a change in the random stream, and measured on the step 4 type I rows a single inserted cell moved 33 of 40 shared cells

checks.question: is the paired drift distributed as noise rather than as a shift, and is the verdict stable at a band wider than the Monte Carlo error?
checks.tolerance_note: the criterion is on the DISTRIBUTION of the paired z, not on every cell individually. Requiring all 160 cells inside two errors would fail about 95 per cent of the time even on perfect data, so it cannot distinguish noise from drift.
checks.why_it_matters: this is the block that answers the journal's "well tested" requirement for the calibration claim. The quantity being certified is that the reported rates do not move when the budget doubles, which is a statement about the spread of the drift and not about any single cell

checks.question: is the paired error strictly smaller, and does its ratio match the closed form sqrt(A / (2A + B))?
checks.why_it_matters: the ratio is the price of nesting. At equal rates the unpaired error is sqrt(3) times the paired one, so a check written against the unpaired value would tolerate a drift up to 73 per cent larger than the data support

checks.question: do shared cells keep bit-identical delta_tip and observed risks on the refined grid?
checks.why_it_matters: nothing is sampled in this block, so any difference on a shared cell is a defect in the join, not noise

checks.question: do the minimum and maximum delta_tip move when the p0 and se axes are halved in step?

monotonicity.consequence: delta_tip is monotone in each axis, so its extremes over a box are attained at the vertices; inserting midpoints of p0 and se adds no vertex, so the extremes cannot move. Verified numerically below rather than only argued.

checks.why_it_matters: the extremes are what a reader quotes as the range of the threshold. Because delta_tip is monotone in each axis they are attained at the vertices, and halving an axis adds no vertex -- so this is a derived consequence, not a lucky observation

checks.question: does pooling over twice as many cells move the type I error by more than the two pooled Monte Carlo errors?
checks.why_it_matters: the pooled type I error is the calibration claim of the whole evaluation. If it moved under grid refinement the headline would be an artefact of the step size chosen in step 1

checks.question: is the per-cell drift centred on zero with unit spread?
checks.why_it_matters: a non-zero mean would be a directional effect hidden by pooling; an sd far below one would mean the quoted per-cell Monte Carlo errors are too wide

checks.question: with twice the bisection iterations and twice the replicates, does the located crossing move less than 0.2 pp?
checks.why_it_matters: delta_sig is the only headline quantity that is estimated rather than derived, so it is the only one whose value depends on the simulation budget

checks.question: is the achieved bracket width already far below the 0.2 pp tolerance, so the residual shift is Monte Carlo?
checks.why_it_matters: the two are routinely conflated. Bisection to 2^-26 of a 20 pp bracket is about 3e-7 pp, so essentially all movement at this budget is Monte Carlo, and the honest statement is that delta_sig is replicate-limited, not locator-limited

checks.question: is the boundary of this step recorded?
checks.statement: doubling replicates and halving a step move an estimate towards its own Monte Carlo expectation. Neither tests whether the two-parameter measurement model is the right one, and neither speaks to the direction of any bias. This step supports the claim that the reported numbers are reproducible; it does not support a claim that they are right.
not_tested: behaviour of layer B, which is analytic only
